issue_context.title: Feature request: coexistence of `ragged` and `output_sequence_length` in `TextVectorization`
issue_context.body:
Sometimes, we may want a ragged tensor but still get to truncate a too long sentence. This configuration is currently forbidden for no reasons.

https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/b3ffea6602dbbb481e82312baa24fe657de83e11/keras/layers/preprocessing/text_vectorization.py#L353-L358
comments: Assign to Matt for further triage.

No strong feeling here. Seems slightly confusing that `output_sequence_length` would effectively work as `max_sequence_length` when `ragged=True`, but definitely something we could document and could be useful.

Seems our options:
1) Allow `ragged=True` and `output_sequence_length=xx`, document the `output_sequence_length` will truncate in the ragged case.
2) Continue to disallow. Users can simply do `text_vectorization(inputs)[:, :max_length]` to truncate.

I'm open to a PR if someone wanted to put one up. @fchollet any strong opinions?
would like to work on it
Yes we can allow it. It's not a big problem. If someone wants to send out a PR we'll review it.

> Yes we can allow it. It's not a big problem. If someone wants to send out a PR we'll review it.

Thank you. Will work on it.
@mattdangerw @fchollet please have a look at the PR https://github.com/keras-team/keras/pull/18980 and let me know your thoughts.

review_comments: Can you add a simple unit test to check that this behavior is verified?

I am unable to pass this simple test:
```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(
        backend.backend() != "tensorflow", reason="Requires ragged tensors."
    )
    def test_ragged_tensor(self):
        layer = layers.TextVectorization(
            output_mode="int",
            vocabulary=["baz", "bar", "foo"],
            ragged=True,
        )
        input_data = [["foo baz baz bar"], ["foo baz bar"], ["foo baz"], ["foo"]]
        output = layer(input_data)
        assert isinstance(output, tf.RaggedTensor)
```

Fails with:
```bash
>       assert isinstance(output, tf.RaggedTensor)
E       AssertionError: assert False
E        +  where False = isinstance(<tf.Tensor: shape=(4, 4), dtype=int64, numpy=\narray([[4, 2, 2, 3],\n       [4, 2, 3, 0],\n       [4, 2, 0, 0],\n       [4, 0, 0, 0]], dtype=int64)>, <class 'tensorflow.python.ops.ragged.ragged_tensor.RaggedTensor'>)
E        +    where <class 'tensorflow.python.ops.ragged.ragged_tensor.RaggedTensor'> = tf.RaggedTensor

keras\layers\preprocessing\text_vectorization_test.py:120: AssertionError
=============================================== short test summary info ===============================================
FAILED keras/layers/preprocessing/text_vectorization_test.py::TextVectorizationTest::test_ragged_tensor - AssertionError: assert False
```
I expected a ```RaggedTensor``` with shape ```(4,None)```, but the layer returns a ```Tensor``` with shape ```(4,4)```.

However the same test passes on Colab. Can you help?
It is looking to me like the layer as it is currently implemented is simply not wired to return ragged tensors.
Address in #19028 that I started independently for another fix for Text Vectorization and also updated it to address issues here.
